title: Descriptive adjectives, agreement and colours
goal: By the end of this lesson you can make adjectives agree in gender and number, place them before or after the noun, name the colours, and use everyday Quebec judgments like c'est le fun, c'est plate and c'est beau.

body: A French adjective takes the gender and number of the noun it describes. The basic rule: add *-e* for feminine, *-s* for plural, *-es* for feminine plural.

Adding *-e* often makes a silent final consonant audible: *petit* [puh-TEE] → *petite* [puh-TEET], *grand* → *grande*. If the adjective already ends in *-e*, the feminine doesn't change: *rouge, jeune, facile*.
learn.tip: A mixed group (masculine + feminine) takes the masculine plural: Paul et Julie sont grands.

body: Some endings change more than just adding -e. Learn these families; they cover hundreds of adjectives.
A few very common adjectives are irregular: *beau / belle*, *nouveau / nouvelle*, *vieux / vieille*, *blanc / blanche*, *long / longue*, *gentil / gentille*.
Most adjectives go AFTER the noun, unlike English: *une voiture rouge* (a red car), *un homme intéressant*. Colours and nationalities always go after.

A small group of short, common adjectives goes BEFORE the noun. Remember BAGS: Beauty (*beau, joli*), Age (*jeune, vieux, nouveau*), Goodness (*bon, mauvais*), Size (*petit, grand, gros*): *une belle maison, un petit chat, un bon café*.
Before a masculine noun starting with a vowel, *beau, nouveau, vieux* become *bel, nouvel, vieil*: *un bel appartement, un vieil ami*.
learn.tip: BAGS adjectives go before: un grand appartement, une jolie robe.

body: Colours are adjectives and agree: *une robe verte, des yeux bleus*. Colours that come from nouns (*orange, marron*) don't change: *des chaussures orange*.
In Quebec, 'brown' is usually *brun* (*des yeux bruns*, *un manteau brun*); *marron* is more common in France.

learn.h: Quebec: c'est le fun, c'est plate, c'est beau
body: Quebecers judge things with a few very frequent expressions. *C'est le fun* = it's fun (*le fun* works like an adjective: *une soirée le fun*). Its opposite is *C'est plate* = it's boring.

*C'est beau* can mean 'it's beautiful', but in Quebec it very often means 'OK, that's fine': *Je vais être en retard. — C'est beau!* *C'est bon* = it tastes good / it's fine. *Fin / fine* = nice, kind. All casual, but used by everyone.

examples.en: I live in a beautiful apartment.

examples.fr: Il est heureux et elle est heureuse.

examples.en: I'm looking for a white tuque.

examples.fr: Le party est vraiment le fun!

quebec.intro: Everyday Quebec judgments: c'est le fun (it's fun), c'est plate (it's boring), c'est beau (it's fine / OK), c'est bon. Fin / fine means nice, and brun is the usual word for brown.

items.note: informal; plate is invariable in speech
informal: le fun used as an adjective

drills.why: beau → bel before a masculine noun starting with a vowel.

drills.en: I'm looking for a white tuque.

drills.why: beau → belle; BAGS: before the noun.

drills.a: Le party est vraiment le fun!

drills.why: brun in Quebec, marron in France.

vocab.ex: Un bel hôtel, une belle ville.

pron.tip: puh-TEE / puh-TEET: the -e makes the t heard.
say luh FONN: Quebecers say 'fonne', not the English 'fun'.

dialogue.fr: Bonjour! Je cherche une tuque pour l'hiver.
dialogue.en: Hello! I'm looking for a tuque for the winter.

dialogue.fr: On a des tuques rouges, bleues et noires.
dialogue.en: We have red, blue and black tuques.

dialogue.fr: La bleue est belle! Elle coûte combien?
dialogue.en: The blue one is nice! How much is it?

dialogue.fr: Vingt-cinq dollars. C'est une bonne tuque, très chaude.
dialogue.en: Twenty-five dollars. It's a good tuque, very warm.

dialogue.fr: Désolé, on a juste des mitaines brunes.
dialogue.en: Sorry, we only have brown mittens.

dialogue.fr: C'est beau, je prends juste la tuque.
dialogue.en: That's fine, I'll just take the tuque.

questions.q: What colour are the available mittens?

speak.prompt: Describe yourself in 3 sentences: height, hair and eye colour, personality.
speak.model: Je suis grand. J'ai les cheveux bruns et les yeux bleus. Je suis sportif et gentil.

speak.prompt: Describe your home and your street with at least four adjectives.
speak.model: J'habite dans un petit appartement. Il est vieux mais beau. La rue est calme et verte.

speak.prompt: Give your opinion on three activities using c'est le fun, c'est plate or c'est beau.
speak.model: Le hockey, c'est le fun! Faire l'épicerie, c'est plate. Le Vieux-Québec, c'est beau!

write.prompt: Write 5–6 sentences describing a friend or family member: appearance, clothes (with colours) and personality. Check every agreement.
write.model: Ma sœur s'appelle Julie. Elle est petite et elle a les cheveux bruns. Elle a les yeux verts. Aujourd'hui, elle porte une tuque rouge et un manteau noir. Elle est très drôle et gentille. Avec elle, c'est toujours le fun!

quiz.q: Which adjective usually goes BEFORE the noun?
quiz.why: BAGS: size adjectives like petit go before.

quiz.q: Which colour does NOT change in the feminine?

quiz.why: Colours from nouns (orange, marron) are invariable.
A mixed group takes the masculine plural.

quiz.q: 'Je vais être en retard. — C'est beau!' means…
quiz.why: In Quebec, c'est beau often means 'that's fine'.

quiz.q: Which is the usual Quebec word for 'brown'?
